correctness.rationale: The proof exhausts rank(A)<d+1, rank(A)=rank(H)=d+1, rank(H)=d+2 without geometry exceptions. Reflecting across a sensor hyperplane proves all-time ambiguity. Full-rank quadratic interpolation reconstructs age, center and unknown mass from one round. Affine-spanning co-spherical arrays give two-round age via a nonzero spatial log ratio except at the circumcenter. There, the strictly increasing shifted harmonic-mean integral eliminates known-mass two-round twins, and the at-most-one-extremum two-age log ratio eliminates unknown-mass three-round twins. A unimodal one-time profile and the strictly folded shifted-profile ratio give sharp ambiguities. Analytic inequalities supply a planar witness. An executed deterministic standard-library checker passed 34099 exact and numerical assertions. Finite tests are not represented as infinite proofs; all quantifiers and boundaries are treated in the analytical proof.

originality.rationale: Within the inspected source and claim history, the previously known d+1-sensor diffusion localization method uses temporal derivatives, quadrature or many samples, not a universal minimal count for raw finite snapshots and mass-calibration status. The published unknown-diffusivity all-time cospherical obstruction cannot imply a known-diffusivity two/three-snapshot theorem. The prior known-age unknown-tensor polynomial recovery does not cover the unknown-age spherical middle rank. Non-spherical single-time recovery is conventional; the novel assessed mathematical statement is the sharp spherical 2-vs-3 transition together with a full geometry/time-count phase diagram. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: An exact all-geometry minimal temporal sampling diagram answers a concrete sensor-versus-clock-versus-mass-calibration design question for an impulsive pollution plume: d+1 co-spherical full-span sensors require 2 known-mass rounds but 3 unknown-mass rounds; d+2 nonspherical sensors need just one; all temporally oversampled coplanar arrays fail. The central-source degeneracy and strict global minimality are scientifically material, not mere parameter renaming. This precisely defines what calibration buys and when time cannot replace geometry. The scope is expressly an idealized mathematical benchmark, not a practical atmospheric deployment claim.
